intro: Biggest rank disagreements between the SEI board and SP+, 2026 season: from the SP+ top 15 and from our own top 15.

teams.explanation: SP+ sits at #50 because the scoreboard says middle-class: +49 margin, #30 nationally, with a 34-18 opener over an FCS team and a 23-29 loss at Indiana dragging the average. SEI reads the plays instead. The Wildcats turn drives into touchdowns at an elite clip (TD% +1.70 SD, red-zone TD% +1.61) and they did it at Penn State, 34-13. The one feature SP+ seems to price hard is discipline — penalty z -1.65, worst on this list. Process over results, exactly where the two boards split.
hints: Process outran scoreboard: margin rank #30 (margin +49) but SEI #4.

teams.explanation: A +7 margin (#61) makes SP+ call Kentucky #44. Our board calls it #15 because of what the defense does to drives: opponent drives end in a fumble or interception at the country's best rates (+2.43 and +1.93 SD) and the defense's first-down PPA is +1.80. It showed up at South Carolina, where a 35-34 win came from the ball coming back over and over. It did not show up in the 17-45 beating at Alabama. The offense is the asterisk: third-down PPA -1.97, SEI offense #37. Kentucky is a takeaway machine with an average passing attack bolted on.
hints: Process outran scoreboard: margin rank #61 (margin +7) but SEI #15.
Offense drives the gap: SEI off #37 vs def #7.

teams.explanation: 5-0 and +70 keeps SP+ at #11, but the plays say the wins were closer than the record: Houston by 2, Oregon State by 11. Our offense half sits at #56 — the Red Raiders move the ball at a league-average pace and the margin is carried by field position and takeaways (INT% +2.51) rather than efficiency. Third-down PPA (+1.71) is the one offensive feature that pops. When the one-possession games bounce the other way, this profile is a .500 profile.
hints: Scoreboard outran process: margin rank #17 (margin +70) but SEI #33.
Offense drives the gap: SEI off #56 vs def #24.

teams.explanation: SP+'s #25 tracks the +48 margin and the loss at Mississippi State. SEI is higher because the Tigers blow plays up on both sides — explosiveness +2.02 on offense, +1.64 allowed on defense — and first-down PPA (+1.53) says they move the ball early and often. The 45-17 shellacking at Florida is the profile talking; the 24-31 loss at Mississippi State is where third-and-long inefficiency bit them.
hints: Process outran scoreboard: margin rank #31 (margin +48) but SEI #8.

teams.explanation: SP+ loves the offense (#5); we rank the defense #44 and that is the whole gap. The Ducks' margin is +13 (#56) after the 31-39 loss at Oklahoma State, and their penalty rate is -1.90 — the worst discipline on the board. What is real: third-down PPA on both sides (~+1.8 to +2.0) says Oregon wins the obvious downs. What is not: preventing anything between them, where the mirror features sit near average.
hints: Process outran scoreboard: margin rank #56 (margin +13) but SEI #22.
Defense drives the gap: SEI off #21 vs def #44.

teams.explanation: The only real argument on this list. SP+ has Georgia #1 overall and #1 on both halves; the +130 margin backs it. SEI's offense half agrees (#9, first-down PPA +2.19, TD% +1.71) but the defense half sits at #38 — the Bulldogs have allowed 17 to Arkansas and 14 to Vanderbilt, and their PPA-allowed and TD%-allowed numbers are only league-average. A margin model cannot see an untested defense; an efficiency model can only measure what was tested.
hints: Scoreboard outran process: margin rank #4 (margin +130) but SEI #14.
Defense drives the gap: SEI off #9 vs def #38.

teams.explanation: No real disagreement here: #11 vs #5, both boards see a 5-0 team with +129 margin and balanced halves (SP+ off #8, def #8). The 41-13 win at Clemson is the marquee play, and the efficiency backs the score — first-down PPA +1.78, TD% +1.63. The gap is rounding, not philosophy.

The defense is the board-seller: havoc +3.52 SD — off the chart — second-down PPA allowed +2.61, red-zone defense +2.59. That defense put 51 on Clemson and held Texas A&M to 6. SP+ sits at #10 because the offense's #22 half and the 24-32 loss at Ole Miss pull the margin down. We weight what the pass rush does to opposing drives more than one bad Saturday in Oxford.
hints: Strongest metrics: Havoc +3.52, 2nd PPA +2.61, RZ TD% +2.59.
